questions.question: On selling of 18 pens at Rs.360, there is a loss equal to the cost of 3 pens. What is the cost price of a pen?
questions.questionHtml: On selling of 18 pens at Rs.360, there is a loss equal to the cost of 3 pens. What is the cost price of a pen?
questions.solution:
(C.P. of 18 pens) - (S.P. of 18 pens) = (C.P. of 3 pens)

CP (1 pen)/SP (1 pen) = 18/15 = 6/5

SP (1 pen) = 360/18 = 20

CP of 1 pen = 6/5 × 20 = 24

questions.question: The cost of 3 cups and 5 plates is ₹1,080 and the cost of 2 cups and 4 plates is ₹840. Find the ratio of the cost of a cup to the cost of a plate.
questions.questionHtml: The cost of 3 cups and 5 plates is ₹1,080 and the cost of 2 cups and 4 plates is ₹840. Find the ratio of the cost of a cup to the cost of a plate.
questions.solution:
Then the cost of 1 cup and 1 plate is (1080 - 840) = Rs 240

The cost of  2 plates is 840 - 480 = 360 .The cost of  1 plates is  360 / 2 = Rs 180

questions.question: Aditya buys 300 mangoes for Rs. 1,100. Some of these mangoes are rotten and are thrown away. He sells the remaining mangoes at Rs. 5 each and makes a profit of Rs. 150. Find the percentage of mangoes thrown away.
questions.questionHtml: Aditya buys 300 mangoes for Rs. 1,100. Some of these mangoes are rotten and are thrown away. He sells the remaining mangoes at Rs. 5 each and makes a profit of Rs. 150. Find the percentage of mangoes thrown away.
questions.solution:
Given :

Aditya buys 300 mangoes for Rs. 1,100.

Sells the remaining mangoes at Rs. 5 each and makes a profit of Rs. 150.

Formula Used : 

Profit = SP - CP

Calculation : 

Let the number of mangoes rotten be x.

Profit = 150

⇒ 150 = (300 - x)5 - 1100

⇒ 150 = 1500 - 5x - 1100

⇒ 150 = 400 - 5x

⇒ - 5x = - 250

⇒ x = 50

Percentage of mangoes thrown away = 50/300 × 100 = \(16 \frac{2}{3} \% \)

∴ The correct answer is  \(16 \frac{2}{3} \% \).

questions.question: A discount of 30% on the marked price of a book enables Arun to get a pen worth Rs. 60 free. How much did Arun pay for the book?
questions.questionHtml: A discount of 30% on the marked price of a book enables Arun to get a pen worth Rs. 60 free. How much did Arun pay for the book?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The 30% discount on the Marked Price is equivalent to the value of the free pen.

⇒ 30% of Marked Price = ₹60

⇒ 1% of Marked Price = ₹2

Arun pays 100% − 30% = 70% of the Marked Price for the book.

⇒ Amount paid = 70 × 2 = ₹140.

∴ The correct answer is ₹140.

Alternate Method

Given: Discount % = 30%, Discount Value = ₹60 (Value of the free pen).

Formula Used: Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) − Discount; Discount = (Discount% ÷ 100) × MP.

⇒ Discount = 30% of MP = 60

⇒ (30 ÷ 100) × MP = 60

⇒ MP = (60 × 100) ÷ 30

⇒ MP = ₹200

⇒ Amount paid (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ Amount paid = 200 − 60 = ₹140

∴ The correct answer is ₹140.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the label of an article. Discount is always calculated on this price.

Selling Price (SP)

The actual price paid by the customer after deducting the discount from the MP. SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Discount Percentage

The ratio of discount to the marked price expressed as a percentage. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Net Profit with Discount

Profit = SP − CP. If an item is marked up by M% and discounted by D%, net profit % = M − D − (MD ÷ 100).

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a 10% discount on dairy products and still manages to make a 20% profit. What is the actual cost (in Rs.) to the shopkeeper of a dairy product marked Rs. 420?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper offers a 10% discount on dairy products and still manages to make a 20% profit. What is the actual cost (in Rs.) to the shopkeeper of a dairy product marked Rs. 420?
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked Price (MP) = ₹420

Discount = 10%

Profit = 20%

Formula used:

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) - Discount

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 + Profit%)

Calculation:

Discount Amount = 10% of 420

⇒ Discount Amount = 0.10 × 420 = ₹42

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) - Discount Amount

⇒ SP = 420 - 42 = ₹378

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit%)

⇒ CP = 378 / (1 + 0.20)

⇒ CP = 378 / 1.20

⇒ CP = ₹315

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 60 pencils at a rate of 4 for Rs. 5 and another 60 pencils at a rate of 2 for Rs. 3. He mixed all the pencils and sold them at a rate of 3 for Rs. 4. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought 60 pencils at a rate of 4 for Rs. 5 and another 60 pencils at a rate of 2 for Rs. 3. He mixed all the pencils and sold them at a rate of 3 for Rs. 4. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
The average cost price of both pencils = \({5\over 4} +{3\over 2} \over 2\) = \(11\over 8\) 

Selling price of pencils = \(4\over 3\)

Loss = \(11\over 8\) - \(4\over 3\) = \(1\over 24\)

Loss % = \(1\over 24\) × \(8\over 11\) × 100 = 3\(1\over 33\)%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper mixes 15 kg of sugar costing ₹ 11/kg with 22 kg of sugar costing ₹12/kg. What is the cost (in ₹) per kg of the mixture? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper mixes 15 kg of sugar costing ₹ 11/kg with 22 kg of sugar costing ₹12/kg. What is the cost (in ₹) per kg of the mixture? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
Given:

15 kg of sugar costing ₹11/kg

22 kg of sugar costing ₹12/kg

Formula used:

Cost per kg of mixture = \(\dfrac{(15 \times 11) + (22 \times 12)}{15 + 22}\)

Calculation:

Cost per kg of mixture = \(\dfrac{(15 \times 11) + (22 \times 12)}{15 + 22}\)

⇒ Cost per kg of mixture = \(\dfrac{165 + 264}{37}\)

⇒ Cost per kg of mixture = \(\dfrac{429}{37}\)

⇒ Cost per kg of mixture = 11.59

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: A seller sells oranges at the rate of 10 for Rs. 28, gaining thereby 40%. For how much did he buy a dozen oranges?
questions.questionHtml: A seller sells oranges at the rate of 10 for Rs. 28, gaining thereby 40%. For how much did he buy a dozen oranges?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total orange = 10

Selling price = Rs. 28

Profit% = 40%

Formula used:

Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

Solution:

Let, cost price = CP

40 = (28 - CP)/CP x 100

40 = [(28/CP) - 1] x 100

40/100 = (28/ CP) - 1

0.4 + 1 = 28/CP

CP = 28/1.4 = 20

Cost price for 10 orange = 20Rs.

Cost price for 1 orang = 2 Rs.

1 Dozen = 12 orange = 2 x 12 = 24Rs.

He will use 24Rs. to buy 12 oranges.

questions.questionHtml: On selling 26 balls for Rs. 1,350, there is a loss equal to the cost price of eight balls. The cost price of a ball is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling Price = Rs. 1350

Calculation:

Let the cost price of one ball be x

Now selling 26 balls for Rs. 1,350, there is a loss equal to the cost price of eight balls

Cost price of 26 balls = 26x, loss = 8x(8 balls)

Loss = Cost Price – Selling Price

⇒ 18x = 1350

⇒ x = 75 

∴ The cost price of a ball is Rs.75

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 13.25%. Had it been sold for Rs.76.70 more, the profit would have been 16.2%. 20% of the cost price of the article (in Rs.) is:
questions.questionHtml: An article is sold at a profit of 13.25%. Had it been sold for Rs.76.70 more, the profit would have been 16.2%. 20% of the cost price of the article (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
Formula:

SP = CP + P, where

SP = Selling price

CP = Cost Price

P = Profit

Calculations:

Let the cost price be Rs 100.

SP for 13.25% profit = Rs 100 + 13.25 = Rs 113.25

SP for 16.2% profit = Rs 100 + 16.20 = Rs 116.20

Difference in profit = Rs 116.20 - Rs 113.25 = Rs 2.95

 

⇒ x = \(76.7× 100 \over 2.95\) = Rs 2600

⇒ 20% of x = 0.2 × Rs 2600 = Rs 520

∴ 20% of the cost price is Rs 520.

questions.question: A fruit seller purchased 300 bananas at the rate of ₹18 per dozen and sold 200 bananas at the rate of ₹24 per dozen and the remaining bananas at the rate of ₹21 per dozen. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: A fruit seller purchased 300 bananas at the rate of ₹18 per dozen and sold 200 bananas at the rate of ₹24 per dozen and the remaining bananas at the rate of ₹21 per dozen. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Given:

The Cost Price (CP) of 300 bananas at = ₹18 per dozen

The Selling Price (SP1) of 200 bananas at = ₹24 per dozen

The Selling Price (SP2) of remaining bananas at = ₹21 per dozen.

Concept used:

Profit% = \(SP - CP\over CP\) × 100

Calculations:

According to the question,

12 banana = 1 dozen

⇒ 300 banana = 300/12 = 25 dozens

Cost Price of 25 dozens = 25 × 18 = Rs. 450

He Sold 200 bananas at Rs. 24 per dozen

⇒ 200 bananas = 200/12 = 16.66 dozens

Cost price of 16.66 dozens of bananas = 16.66 × 24

⇒ Rs. 399.84 ~ Rs. 400

He Sold 100 bananas at Rs. 21 per dozen

⇒ 100 bananas = 100/12 = 8.33 dozens

Cost price of 8.33 dozens of bananas = 8.33 × 21

⇒ Rs. 174.93 ~ Rs. 175

Net Selling Price = 400 + 175 = Rs. 575

Net Profit% = [(575 - 450)/(450)] × 100

⇒ Net Profit% = [125/450] × 100

⇒ Net Profit% = 0.2777 × 100 = 27.77% or ​​​​\(27\frac{7}{9}\%\)​​​

∴ ​​​His net profit percentage = 27.77% or ​​​​\(27\frac{7}{9}\%\)​ .

questions.question: Sonam purchased a mobile phone for ₹27,000 and sold it at a loss of 19%. With that money she purchased a Tablet and sold it at a gain of 20%. What is her overall gain or loss?
questions.questionHtml: Sonam purchased a mobile phone for ₹27,000 and sold it at a loss of 19%. With that money she purchased a Tablet and sold it at a gain of 20%. What is her overall gain or loss?
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost price of the mobile phone = Rs. 27000

The loss% = 19%

Formula used:

SP = CP × {1 + (Profit % / 100)} = CP × {1 - (Loss % / 100)}

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Calculation:

According to the question

The selling price of mobile phone = \(({1-{19\over100}})\ × 27000 = 21870\)

The selling price of tablet = \(({1+{20\over100}})× 21870= 1.2×26244 = 26244\)

The loss = 27000 - 26244 = 756

∴ The required result will be "loss 756".

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 20 kg of sugar at Rs. 45 per Kg., 25 kg of sugar at Rs. 50 per kg and 35 kg of sugar at Rs. 40 per kg. He spent a sum of Rs. 450 on transportation and other expenses. He mixed all three types of sugar and sold all the stocks at Rs. 52.50 per kg. His profit percent in the entire transaction is:
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper bought 20 kg of sugar at Rs. 45 per Kg., 25 kg of sugar at Rs. 50 per kg and 35 kg of sugar at Rs. 40 per kg. He spent a sum of Rs. 450 on transportation and other expenses. He mixed all three types of sugar and sold all the stocks at Rs. 52.50 per kg. His profit percent in the entire transaction is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Rate of sugar of quantity 1 = Rs. 45

Quantity = 20 kg

Rate of sugar of quantity 2 = Rs. 50

Quantity = 25 kg

Rate of sugar of quantity 3 = Rs. 40

Quantity = 35 kg

Money spent on transportation and other expenses = Rs. 450

Selling price of mixed sugar = Rs. 52.50

Formula used:

Profit = SP – CP

Profit%= (Profit/CP) × 100

Calculation:

CP of sugar of quantity 1 = 45 × 20

⇒ 900

CP of sugar of quantity 2 = 50 × 25

⇒ 1250

CP of sugar of quantity 3 = 40 × 35

⇒ 1400

Total quantity of mixes sugar = (20 + 25 + 35)

⇒ 80

Final CP including transportation and other expenses = (900 + 1250 + 1400 + 450)

⇒ 4000

CP of 1 kg of mixed sugar = 4000/80

⇒ 50

SP of 1 kg of mixed sugar = 52.50

Profit = (52.50 – 50)

⇒ 2.50

Profit% = (2.50/50 × 100)

⇒ 5%

∴ His profit percentage in the entire transaction is 5%

questions.question: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 70% of this price, then there is a loss of 10%. What is the percentage profit, when it is sold at the original selling price?
questions.questionHtml: An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 70% of this price, then there is a loss of 10%. What is the percentage profit, when it is sold at the original selling price?
questions.solution:
Let the article be originally sold for Rs. 900.

If it is sold at 70% of this price, the selling price would be ⇒ 900 × 70% = Rs. 630

So, the cost price of the article = 630 ÷ 0.9 = Rs. 700

Now, the profit% when it's sold at the original selling price = \({{900 - 700} \over 700} \times 100\%\) ⇒ \(​\frac{200}{7}\)%

questions.question: Harsh purchased a scooter for ₹48,000. He sold it at a loss of 15%. With that money he purchased another scooter and sold it at a profit of 22.5%. What is his overall loss/profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: Harsh purchased a scooter for ₹48,000. He sold it at a loss of 15%. With that money he purchased another scooter and sold it at a profit of 22.5%. What is his overall loss/profit percentage?
questions.solution:
First S.P = \(\frac{(100-15)}{100}×48,000\) ⇒ Rs. 40,800 = Second C.P

Second S.P = \(\frac{(100+22.5)}{100}×40,800\) = Rs. 49,980

Total profit = Second S.P - C.P = 49,980 - 48,000 = 1,980

Profit % = \(\frac{1,980}{48,000}×100\) = 0.04125 × 100 = 4.125 %

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹425.25, there is a loss of 5.5%. If the same article is sold for ₹465.75, then what is the profit per cent?
questions.questionHtml: By selling an article for ₹425.25, there is a loss of 5.5%. If the same article is sold for ₹465.75, then what is the profit per cent?
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling price = Rs. 425.25

Loss = 5%

Formula used:

Selling price = Cost price - Loss

Profit = Selling price - Cost price, when selling price > cost price.

Profit % = (Profit/cost price) × 100

Calculation:

Let the cost price is Rs.x

Selling price = x - 5.5% of x

⇒ 425.25 = 94.5x/100

⇒ (425.25 × 100)/94.5 = x

⇒ 450 = x

Cost price is Rs. 450

Profit = Rs.(465.75 - 450)

⇒ 15.75

Profit % = (15.75/450) × 100

⇒ 3.5%

∴ Profit percentage is 3.5%.

A + B = 15 kg    ----(equation 1)

questions.question: A sells an article to B at 20% loss, who further sells it to C at 18% profit. Later on, C sells it to D at 10% profit. If C has a profit of ₹944, then how much is the loss to A?
questions.questionHtml: A sells an article to B at 20% loss, who further sells it to C at 18% profit. Later on, C sells it to D at 10% profit. If C has a profit of ₹944, then how much is the loss to A?
questions.solution:
Given:

 A sells at a losss of 20%

B sells at a profit of 18%

C sells at a profit of 10%

C's profit = Rs. 944

Formula used:

Loss = Cost price - Selling price, when cost price > selling price

Profit = Selling price - Cost price, when selling price > cost price

Calculation:

Let the cost price is Rs. x

Selling price of A = x - 20% of x

⇒ 80% of x

Selling price of B = 80% of x + 18% of 80% of x

⇒ (80x/100) + (1440x/10000)

⇒ (8000x + 1440x)/10000

⇒ 9440x/10000

Cost price for  C = 9440x/10000

⇒ 0.944x

C's profit = 10%

10% of 0.944x = 944

⇒ (10 × 0.944x/100) = 944

x = (944 × 100)/(0.944 × 10)

x = 10,000

Loss to A = 10,000 × 20%

⇒ 2000

∴ Loss to A is Rs. 2000.

questions.question: An article is sold at a profit of 30%. If both cost price and selling price of the article are decreased by Rs.100, the profit now would be 45%. The original cost price of the article is:
questions.questionHtml: An article is sold at a profit of 30%. If both cost price and selling price of the article are decreased by Rs.100, the profit now would be 45%. The original cost price of the article is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Old profit = 30%

New profit = 45%

Formula used:

\(\;Profit\% \; = \;\frac{{SP\; - \;CP}}{{CP}}\; \times 100\)

Calculation:

Let the original cost price of the article be X.

Old selling price at 30% profit will be = \(\frac{{130}}{{100}}\;x\)

⇒ 1.3x

both cost price and selling price of the article are decreased by Rs.100

∴ New CP = x -100 and new SP = 1.3x - 100

\(\;Profit\% \; = \;\frac{{SP\; - \;CP}}{{CP}}\; \times 100\)

 

\(45\; = \;\frac{{\left( {1.3x\; - \;100} \right)\; - \;\left( {x\; - \;100} \right)}}{{x\; - \;100}}\; \times \;100\;\)

⇒ 0.45x - 45 = 1.3x - 100 - x + 100

⇒ 0.45x - 0.3x = 45

⇒ 0.15x = 45

x = 300

The original cost price is 300

questions.question: A certain quantity of rice was bought for Rs. x and sold for Rs. y, thereby earning a profit of 25%. Had the cost price been 20% less and the selling price been Rs. 58 less, a profit of 20% would have been earned. Find the value of x.
questions.questionHtml: A certain quantity of rice was bought for Rs. x and sold for Rs. y, thereby earning a profit of 25%. Had the cost price been 20% less and the selling price been Rs. 58 less, a profit of 20% would have been earned. Find the value of x.
questions.solution:
Given:

Cost price, CP = Rs x

Selling price, SP = Rs y

Profit % = 25%

Concept used:

SP = CP × (100 + P)%

Calculation:

SP = CP  × (100 + P%)

y = x × (125/100)

y= 5x/4      ----(1)

The new cost price = 80% of x

The new selling price = y - 58

Then, (y - 58) = 80% × x × (100 + 20)%      ----(2)

Putting (1) in (2),

questions.questionHtml: By selling an article for Rs. 640, a person loses 15% of its selling price. At what price (in Rs.) should he sell it to gain 15% on its cost price?
questions.solution:

The selling price of an article = Rs. 640

Loss = 15% of SP

Gain = 15% of CP

Formula used:

Gain% = (SP – CP)/CP × 100

Loss% = (CP – SP)/CP × 100

Calculation:

The SP of an article is Rs. 640

According to the question

⇒ 736 + 110.4

⇒ 846.40

questions.question: A person bought 60 books for Rs. 60 each. He sold 50 of them at a loss of 4%. At what per cent profit should be sell the remaining books so that he gains 5% in the entire transaction?
questions.questionHtml: A person bought 60 books for Rs. 60 each. He sold 50 of them at a loss of 4%. At what per cent profit should be sell the remaining books so that he gains 5% in the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
Ans: 4

Given:

A person bought 60 books for Rs. 60 each.

He sold 50 of them at a loss of 4%. 

Formula used:

Cost price × (100 + Profit %)/100 = Selling price

Also, Cost price × (100 - Loss %)/100 = Selling price

Calculation:

Cost price of 60 books = 60 × 60 = 3600 Rs.

Cost price of 50 books = 50 × 60 = 3000 Rs.

Selling price for 50 books = 3000 × 96/100 = 2880 Rs.

Selling price for the whole transaction, when all books sold at 5% profit = 3600 × 105/100 = 3780 Rs.

Remaining books no. is = 10

Cost price of 10 books = 60 × 10 = 600 Rs.

Selling price for the 10 books to fulfill the condition of 5% profit on whole transaction = 3780 - 2880 = 900 Rs.

Profit on remaining 10 books = \(\frac{{900 - 600}}{{600}}\)× 100 = \(\frac{{300}}{{600}}\)× 100 = 50%

∴ Remaining 10 books should be sold at 50% profit

Shortcut Trick

Let profit at remaining 10 books is A%

Fraction of 50 books in 60 books = 5/6

Fraction of 10 books in 60 books = 1/6

Fraction of one deal × profit/loss in % + Fraction of other deal × profit/loss in % = Final result (profit/loss)

we will take (+)ve sign for profit and (-)ve sign for loss

⇒ 5/6 × (-4) + 1/6 × A = 5

⇒ A/6 = 5 + 20/6

⇒ A/6 = 50/6

⇒ A = 50%

questions.question: An article is marked at a price that is 20% more than its cost price. After allowing a certain discount on the marked price, the profit reduces to 10%. The discount percentage is
questions.questionHtml: An article is marked at a price that is 20% more than its cost price. After allowing a certain discount on the marked price, the profit reduces to 10%. The discount percentage is
questions.solution:
Given:

An article is marked at a price that is 20% more than its cost price. After allowing a certain discount on the marked price, the profit reduces to 10%. 

Concept used:

Profit and Loss

Calculation:

Let the Cost price of an article be Rs.100

An article is marked at a price that is 20% more than its cost price.

CP : MP = 100 : 120

CP : MP = 5 : 6  - - - (i) 

Profit reduces to 10%

CP : SP = 100 : 110

CP : SP = 10 : 11 - - - (ii)

Equating the values of CP in both the equations

Multiply equation (i) with 2

CP : MP = 5 × 2 : 6 × 2

CP : MP = 10 : 12

MP : CP : SP = 120 : 100 : 110

Mark price - Selling price = Discount

Discount % = \(\frac{{{\rm{Discount}}}}{{{\rm{Markup}}}} \times 100\)

Discount % =  \(\frac{{120\ -\ 110}}{{120}} \times 100\)

Discount % = \(\frac{{25}}{3} = 8\frac{1}{3}\% \)

questions.question: A retailer marks up the price of his goods by 30%. He sells 50% of his goods at a discount of 8% and the remaining at a discount of 6%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A retailer marks up the price of his goods by 30%. He sells 50% of his goods at a discount of 8% and the remaining at a discount of 6%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Given:

Marked price = 130% of cost price

Discount% = 8% & 6% for 50% goods

Formula used:

Marked price = [Marked% / 100] x CP

Selling price = [Discount% / 100] x MP

Profit % = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100

Profit = SP - CP

Solution:

Let, cost price = CP 

So, marked price = 130/100 x CP = 1.3CP

The selling price of 50% goods at an 8% discount = \([{{{(100-8) \over 100} \times 1.3CP} \over 2}]\)

= 0.46 x 1.3CP = 0.598CP

The selling price of 50% goods at a 6% discount = \([{{{(100-6) \over 100} \times 1.3CP} \over 2}]\)

= 0.47 x 1.3CP = 0.611CP

Total selling price = (0.598+0.611)CP = 1.209CP

Profit = SP - CP = 1.209CP - CP = 0.209CP

Profit% = [0.209CP / CP] x 100 = 20.9%

Shortcut Trick

Concept Used:

Weighted average for profit calculations.

Calculation:

Assume cost price of goods = 100 units

Markup = 30% of cost price

⇒ Marked price = 130 units

Selling price of first half of goods = 92% of marked price (due to 8% discount)

⇒ Effective selling price for this half = 0.92 × 130 = 119.6 units

Selling price of second half of goods = 94% of marked price (due to 6% discount)

⇒ Effective selling price for this half = 0.94 × 130 = 122 units

The average selling price (considering equal quantity sold at both discounts)

⇒ (119.6 + 122) / 2 = 120.8 units

Profit percentage = ((Selling price - Cost price) / Cost price) × 100

⇒ Profit percentage = ((120.8 - 100) / 100) × 100 = 20.9%

Therefore, the retailer makes a profit of 20.9%.

questions.question: A businessman marks up the price of his goods by 25% and gives a discount of 5% to the customer. He also uses a 950 gm weight instead of a 1000 gm weight. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A businessman marks up the price of his goods by 25% and gives a discount of 5% to the customer. He also uses a 950 gm weight instead of a 1000 gm weight. Find his overall profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the Successive Ratio Method (CP : SP):

Markup of 25% ⇒ 4 : 5

Discount of 5% ⇒ 20 : 19

False weight (950g instead of 1000g) ⇒ 950 : 1000 = 19 : 20

Overall Ratio (CP : SP) = (4 × 20 × 19) : (5 × 19 × 20) = 4 : 5

Overall Profit % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup = 25%, Discount = 5%, False weight = 950 gm, True weight = 1000 gm

Formula Used:

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1 gm be ₹1. So, CP of 1000 gm = ₹1000.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) for 1000 gm = 1000 + 25% of 1000 = ₹1250.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) after 5% discount = 1250 − (5% of 1250) = 1250 − 62.5 = ₹1187.5.

⇒ The shopkeeper gives only 950 gm, so Actual CP = 950 × 1 = ₹950.

⇒ Profit = SP − Actual CP = 1187.5 − 950 = ₹237.5.

⇒ Profit % = (237.5 ÷ 950) × 100 = 25%.

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses a false weight, Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.

Effective Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is given by: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100. Use positive sign for profit/markup and negative for loss/discount.

Relation between MP, SP and CP

Marked Price (MP) is always marked above the Cost Price (CP). Discounts are always calculated on the MP to get the Selling Price (SP). SP = MP × (1 − Discount ÷ 100).

questions.question: A trader marked a table at ₹37,062, and sold it allowing a 33% discount. If his profit was 42%, then the cost price (in ₹) of the table was:
questions.questionHtml: A trader marked a table at ₹37,062, and sold it allowing a 33% discount. If his profit was 42%, then the cost price (in ₹) of the table was:
questions.solution:
Given:

The marked price table = Rs. 37,062

The discount percentage = 33%

The profit = 42%

Formula used:

P = SP - CP     Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

Discount = Marked price - Selling price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the table be X

The selling price = \(37,062× ({1-{33\over100}})=37,062\ × ({100-33\over100})=37,062\ ×({67\over100})\) = 24831.54

The profit is 42% then.

⇒ 42 = \({24831.54\ -\ X\over X}\ ×100\)

⇒ 42X = (24831.54 - X) × 100

⇒ 42X = 2483154 - 100X

⇒ 42X + 100X = 2483154

⇒ 142X = 2483154

⇒ X = \({24,83,154\over142}=17,487\)

∴ The required result will be Rs. 17,487.

questions.question: By selling an article at 66 \(\frac{2}{3}\) % of the actual selling price, a loss of 25% is incurred. What is the profit percentage on selling the article at its actual selling price?
questions.questionHtml: By selling an article at 66\(\frac{2}{3}\)% of the actual selling price, a loss of 25% is incurred. What is the profit percentage on selling the article at its actual selling price?
questions.solution:
Given:

The loss percentage = 25%

Formula used:

P = SP - CP     Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article be C and the selling price of the article be S

According to the question

⇒ \({{2\over 3}S}\ =\ {{3\over 4}{C}}\)

⇒ \({S\ =\ {9\over 8}C}\)     ----(1)

When an article sold on the actual selling price

Profit percentage = \({SP\ -\ CP\over CP}\ \times 100\)

Where, SP = S, and CP = C

⇒ \({S\ -\ C\over C}\ \times 100\)

By equation (1)

⇒ \({{9\over 8}C\ -\ {C}\over C}\ \times 100\)

⇒ \({9\ -\ 8\over 8}\ \times 100\ =\ 12.5\% \)

∴ The required result will be 12.5%.
